title: Streaming Is in the Driver’s Seat; It’s Time to Get Transparency in Gear
summary: This blog explores some of the problems streaming TV providers face, along with a privacy-forward solution that platforms can use to improve their position.
body_text: In 2025, streaming TV overtook linear television in total viewership for the first time in history. This achievement underscored a fundamental shift in how modern audiences find and watch video content. But for digital advertisers, an even more significant moment lies just ahead. Streaming TV is expected to outpace linear in total ad spend by 2028 , according to eMarketer. When that happens, streaming will not only be where the audiences are. It will be where the budget is too. Unfortunately, despite tracking this trend for several years, many streaming TV providers may be underequipped to answer advertiser demand and realize the full value of their supply. This blog will explore some of the problems streaming TV providers face, along with a privacy-forward solution that platforms can use to improve their position for when (not if ) streaming takes the spotlight for good. The Twofold Problem: Media Quality and Data Transparency All media suppliers must deliver on quality metrics while providing as much data transparency as possible. In general, “media quality” refers to several individual metrics that most advertisers use to assess the value of impressions and the success of campaigns. Three of the most important media quality metrics for buyers are: Viewability . Did an ad have an opportunity to be seen? Fraud . Was it viewed by a real person? Suitability . Did it serve in an environment that supported the brand's business values? Regardless of how an advertiser prioritizes media quality, it’s vital to know where an ad was delivered in order to measure performance effectively. That is where data transparency comes in. For streaming TV, data transparency typically comes in two forms: app-level and program-level. App-level transparency refers to the app in which an ad was shown, while program-level transparency drills deeper to the exact content being consumed. This is an essential part of campaign measurement and delivery, but it is something that has been notoriously difficult for suppliers to provide. What’s Obscuring Transparency for Streaming TV? One external obstacle for streaming TV platforms has been long-standing national regulations like the Video Privacy Protection Act (VPPA). Established in 1988, the VPPA is a US privacy law that prevents companies from disclosing personal identifying information about a user’s viewing habits without their informed written consent. While its original intent was to prevent the abuse of VHS cassette rental histories in the 80s and 90s, the law took on new life in the streaming era and was invoked to prevent the measurement of relevant streaming TV data in ad campaigns. Providers also face internal resistance to data transparency from their own audiences. Privacy has become a serious concern for many Internet users in recent years, and it’s fallen on individual companies to answer that concern with policy-backed commitments to protecting private information. That makes the transparency problem an even harder needle to thread. The ideal solution to this problem is one that would provide enough transparency to measure quality without compromising privacy. That is precisely what DV’s latest streaming TV solutions can offer. DV’s Clean Room Integration Bridges the Gap As part of DV’s Certified Transparent Streaming program, DV now offers a Clean Room Integration in which streaming TV providers can share program-level data without compromising privacy requirements . Here’s how it works: Providers submit their data with non-personal identifiers into DV’s Clean Room Integration DV automatically joins the non-personal data with its own to produce standardized media quality and outcome metrics The anonymized data is then distributed to advertiser partners for their measurement and reporting needs Since no personal identifiers are passed on with the content information, DV’s Clean Room Integration is compliant with regulations like the VPPA. It also allows streaming TV providers to take full advantage of DV’s industry-leading measurement capabilities. But perhaps most importantly, it allows streaming TV providers to maintain control of their data and measure media quality in a way that reflects both their own values and those of their audiences. In a few short years, streaming TV will rule the video marketplace in all the metrics that matter to advertisers. But with great power comes great expectations. Advertisers will expect and demand a far more accurate and comprehensive picture of media quality than they are currently getting from the space. If streaming TV is to continue its prime time push, the proper adjustments need to be made now. Luckily, solutions like DV Certified Transparent Streaming and DV Clean Room Integration can handle most of the heavy lifting and help buyers and suppliers continue to build long-lasting and mutually beneficial partnerships together. title: DARPA Taps Array Labs to Advance Distributed Space Architecture
summary: DARPA selects Array Labs to advance simulation and modeling for its distributed radar satellite constellation, supporting development of optimal operating modes.
body_text: PALO ALTO, CA, July 31, 2025 — The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has awarded Array Labs a contract to support modeling and simulation of its distributed radar satellite system. Under this contract, Array will perform high-fidelity simulations to further validate its novel operating modes, which enable a new paradigm of wide-area, high-resolution imagery. These efforts build on Array’s existing body of work supporting its first commercial cluster , launching next year, and extend these techniques to future generations of the system with even greater performance. DARPA’s support brings the vision of a real-time 3D map of the world one step closer. Array’s modeling will focus on how to best configure and scale its constellation to maximize imaging performance, system robustness, and data delivery under real-world conditions. The work builds on existing simulation efforts and helps validate design decisions that will shape how the constellation collects, communicates, and adapts over time. DARPA has long played a defining role in advancing breakthrough technologies with global impact. Its investments helped seed GPS, stealth platforms, driverless cars, orbital Earth imaging, and commercial robotics. “This marks another step in DARPA’s tradition of catalyzing enduring capabilities, not just technologies,” said Andrew Peterson, CEO of Array Labs. “We’re building to that standard: a sensing layer that doesn’t blink, delivering global domain awareness and real-time volumetric intelligence in places legacy systems can’t reach.” Array Labs was recently designated “awardable” by DARPA’s Expedited Research Implementation Series ( ERIS ) Marketplace, a digital platform designed to accelerate acquisition velocity and drive national security innovation. The ERIS listing reflects a deep alignment between Array’s work and DARPA’s strategic priorities.

body_text: For centuries, humans have searched for the secret of eternal life. Ancient legends, modern science, and futuristic technologies have all explored the possibility of escaping ageing and death. While immortality remains impossible for humans, nature has already created a creature with a remarkable survival ability. Deep in the oceans lives a tiny jellyfish called Turritopsis dohrnii , often known as the immortal jellyfish. This small marine animal has developed one of the most fascinating abilities in the natural world. Instead of ageing until death, it can reverse its life cycle and return to a younger stage. This extraordinary process has made the immortal jellyfish one of the most studied creatures in marine biology and a symbol of nature’s incredible ability to adapt. What Is the Immortal Jellyfish? The immortal jellyfish, scientifically named Turritopsis dohrnii , is a species of jellyfish that belongs to the group of animals called hydrozoans. Unlike many other creatures, it has the ability to transform its adult body back into an earlier stage of development. This does not mean the jellyfish cannot die. It can still be eaten by predators, affected by disease, or harmed by environmental changes. However, when it faces severe stress, injury, starvation, or other difficult conditions, it has a unique biological response that allows it to restart its life cycle. The jellyfish is extremely small, usually measuring only a few millimetres across. Despite its tiny size, its survival strategy has attracted worldwide attention from scientists studying ageing, regeneration, and cellular biology. How Does the Jellyfish Reverse Ageing? Most jellyfish follow a predictable life cycle. They begin as larvae, settle onto surfaces as small structures called polyps, and eventually develop into free swimming adult jellyfish. After reproducing, many jellyfish species naturally die. Turritopsis dohrnii follows a similar pattern but has an unusual ability. When threatened by harsh conditions, it can transform its adult body back into a polyp stage. This process is known as cellular transdifferentiation . During this transformation, specialised cells change into different types of cells. The jellyfish shrinks, loses its adult features, and forms a new polyp structure. From there, it can grow into another adult jellyfish with the same genetic information. Scientists describe this ability as a biological reset button. Instead of continuing towards the end of its natural life cycle, the creature returns to an earlier stage and begins again. The Science Behind Nature’s Amazing Survival Trick Cellular transdifferentiation is one of the main reasons the immortal jellyfish is so important to researchers. Understanding how its cells can change roles may provide valuable information about regeneration and biological repair. Scientists are interested in how this tiny creature controls its cells and protects itself from ageing-related damage. The jellyfish’s abilities may help researchers better understand how living organisms maintain healthy cells and respond to injury. However, scientists do not believe that studying the immortal jellyfish will immediately lead to human immortality. Humans and jellyfish are extremely different organisms, and the biological systems involved are far more complex in people. Instead, research into Turritopsis dohrnii helps expand our understanding of life, ageing, and the natural processes that allow some organisms to survive extreme challenges. Where Can Immortal Jellyfish Be Found? Although the immortal jellyfish is small and difficult to spot, it has been discovered in oceans around the world. Researchers have recorded populations in areas including the Mediterranean Sea, parts of the Atlantic Ocean, waters near Japan, and regions around Panama and Brazil. Its ability to spread across different environments shows how adaptable the species can be. However, finding these jellyfish in the wild is challenging because of their tiny size and delicate bodies. There are several recognised species within the Turritopsis group, but Turritopsis dohrnii is currently the species most famous for its life cycle reversal ability. Can the Immortal Jellyfish Live Forever? The word “immortal” can sometimes create misunderstandings. The jellyfish is not impossible to kill. It can still become food for predators or die because of environmental dangers. In controlled laboratory conditions, researchers suggest that the jellyfish may theoretically repeat its life cycle multiple times. However, survival in the wild is much more difficult because ocean ecosystems contain many threats. Its immortality refers mainly to its ability to avoid natural ageing. Instead of dying because of old age, it can return to an earlier developmental stage and continue living. This unique feature makes it different from almost every other known animal species. Why This Tiny Creature Fascinates Humans The idea of reversing ageing has fascinated humanity for thousands of years. Stories about eternal youth and everlasting life appear in cultures across the world. The immortal jellyfish captures human imagination because it represents a real example of biological renewal. While humans experience ageing as a one way process, this tiny ocean creature demonstrates that nature can create completely different approaches to survival. Marine biologists often describe the jellyfish as a reminder of how much remains unknown about life on Earth. Even a creature only a few millimetres long can reveal surprising secrets about biology. Lessons From the Ocean’s Most Remarkable Survivor The immortal jellyfish teaches scientists that ageing and regeneration are not the same across all species. Nature has developed countless survival strategies, many of which are still being discovered. Studying unusual animals like Turritopsis dohrnii helps researchers explore important questions about evolution, adaptation, and the future of biological science. The jellyfish may not provide humans with a path to eternal life, but it offers something equally valuable: knowledge. Its incredible ability to transform itself shows that the natural world still holds many mysteries waiting to be explored. Conclusion The immortal jellyfish is one of the most extraordinary examples of survival found in the oceans. Through cellular transdifferentiation, it can reverse its development and begin its life cycle again, challenging traditional ideas about ageing and death. Although it is not truly impossible to kill, its ability to repeatedly renew itself makes it one of the most fascinating creatures on Earth. This tiny jellyfish proves that even the smallest animals can hold some of nature’s greatest secrets. As scientists continue studying Turritopsis dohrnii, this remarkable creature may help us understand more about cells, regeneration, and the complex processes that shape life itself.
